item.title: OpenAIModel: disable client retries on ApiModel.retryer replays (fixes request multiplication)
item.body:
Closes #3034.

On a rate limit, OpenAIModel and AzureOpenAIModel currently send 9 requests: ApiModel.retryer makes 3 attempts and the openai client inside each one keeps its default max_retries=2.

This change keeps the client's own retries on the first attempt and uses self.client.with_options(max_retries=0) only on the retryer's replays. A 429 now costs 3 + 1 + 1 = 5 requests. 5xx errors, dropped connections and timeouts are unchanged, because the retryer does not retry them and the client's retries are their only retry. Simply setting max_retries=0 on the client would drop those to 1 request (measured: results/e1/smol-openai-mr0/ in the repository below).

Measured against a local fake server, before -> after:
- 429, Retry-After: 1: 9 -> 5 requests
- 500: 3 -> 3
- dropped connection: 3 -> 3
- no answer: 3 -> 3

Tests: two new tests fail before the change and pass after; a third checks the first attempt keeps the client's retries. make quality passes.

Not in scope: how a rate limit is detected (#2186, #2382), and whether the retryer's waits should read Retry-After.

Raw logs and the fault server: https://github.com/simin-yuan/agent-double-exec-bench

AI disclosure: I directed this work. The patch, its tests and the measurements were produced by AI assistants I operate. Every number above is derived from the server logs in the linked repository, and I will answer review comments on it.

issue.title: OpenAIModel: client retries and ApiModel retries multiply (9 requests per rate limit)

repository.name: smolagents
repository.description: 🤗 smolagents: a barebones library for agents that think in code.

issue.body:
### What happens
`OpenAIModel` (and `AzureOpenAIModel`) wraps `client.chat.completions.create` in `ApiModel.retryer`
(3 attempts). The `openai` client inside keeps its default `max_retries=2`. On a 429 every outer attempt
makes 3 requests, so one rate limit costs 9 requests.

### Minimal repro
Any endpoint that always answers `429` with `Retry-After: 1`:

    from smolagents import OpenAIModel
    model = OpenAIModel(model_id="any", api_base="http://127.0.0.1:PORT/v1", api_key="dummy")
    model.generate([{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "hi"}]}])

Measured against a local fake server (main @ 96f33fa, openai 2.54.0, Python 3.13, default settings):

| fault (every request) | now: requests / time to error | with the change below |
|---|---|---|
| 429, Retry-After: 1 | 9 / 835 s | 5 / 600 s |
| 500 | 3 / 16 s | 3 / 17 s |
| connection dropped | 3 / 16 s | 3 / 17 s |
| no answer | 3 / 1816 s | 3 / 1817 s |

Each cell includes about 10 s of Python start-up and framework import (elapsed time minus the step duration
the framework logs); in the 500 and dropped-connection cells the actual call therefore took about 5 s of the 16.
The 429 times vary between runs because the waits are jittered.
Raw logs (`results/e3/before/` and `results/e3/after/`): https://github.com/simin-yuan/agent-double-exec-bench

### Proposed change (small, `OpenAIModel` only)
Keep the client's own retries on the first attempt; on the retryer's replays use
`self.client.with_options(max_retries=0)`. 5xx, connection errors and timeouts behave exactly as today
(only the client retries them); a rate limit costs 3 + 1 + 1 requests instead of 3 × 3.
The OpenAI Agents SDK does the same (`run_internal/model_retry.py`: provider retries stay on for the
first attempt and are switched off on the runner's own replays).

This fixes the request count, not the waiting time: the retryer's two waits (120–240 s, then 240–960 s)
do not read `Retry-After`. Whether they should is a separate question, so I left it out of this change.

Not in scope: how a rate limit is detected. #2186 and #2382 propose status-code detection; one data point
for them: a 500 whose message contains "rate limit" or "429" gets the rate-limit path (9 requests instead of 3),
and the same 429 response whose body does not mention rate limits costs 9 requests through `OpenAIModel`
(the client's message includes "Error code: 429") but 3 through `LiteLLMModel` (its message does not).

I have a patch with tests (they fail before and pass after; `make quality` and the full test suite pass;
log in `upstream/TEST_LOG.txt` of the same repository)
The fix is in #3036.

AI disclosure: I directed this work. The instrumented runs, the patch and its tests were produced by AI
assistants I operate. Every number above is derived from the server logs in the linked repository.

issue.title: `Retrying` ignores `Retry-After`, and the first retry already waits 2–3× `wait_seconds`

repository.name: smolagents
repository.description: 🤗 smolagents: a barebones library for agents that think in code.

issue.body:
## What happens

Two things, checked on `smolagents==1.26.0` and on current `main` (96f33fa).

1. **`Retry-After` is never read.** `grep -ri "retry-after" src/` returns nothing. When a provider answers `429` and says "come back in 3 seconds", the model-level retry sleeps for whatever the exponential schedule says instead.

2. **The first retry waits 2–3× the configured `wait_seconds`.** Is multiplying before the first sleep intended? In `Retrying.__call__` the delay is multiplied by `exponential_base` (plus jitter) and *then* slept, so the first wait is `wait_seconds × 2 × (1 + jitter)` rather than `wait_seconds`. Measured below with `RETRY_WAIT=2`: the first gap between retry groups is **5.16 s**, where the configured value was 2 s.

With the `ApiModel` defaults (`max_attempts=3`, `wait_seconds=60`, `exponential_base=2`, jitter on) this means a single rate-limited call sleeps 120–240 s and then 240–960 s — **6–20 minutes** before it gives up.

## Reproduction

A local OpenAI-compatible server that answers the first *N* `/v1/chat/completions` requests with `429` and a `Retry-After: 3` header, then a normal response; one `OpenAIModel` call through a `ToolCallingAgent`.

```bash
RETRY_WAIT=2 python r429.py     # RETRY_WAIT only scales the waits down so the run finishes quickly
```

Requests the server received for one logical call, with `Retry-After: 3` on every 429:

| # | t (s) | `x-stainless-retry-count` | note |
|---|-------|---------------------------|------|
| 1 | 2.25 | 0 | first request |
| 2 | 5.25 | 1 | 3.00 s later — the openai client *does* honour the header |
| 3 | 8.25 | 2 | 3.00 s later |
| 4 | 13.41 | 0 | **model-level retry: 5.16 s after the previous attempt** |
| 5 | 16.41 | 1 | 3.00 s |
| 6 | 19.41 | 2 | 3.00 s |
| 7 | 34.23 | 0 | **14.82 s later** |
| 8 | 37.23 | 1 | 3.00 s |
| 9 | 40.23 | 2 | 3.00 s |

So: 9 HTTP requests for one logical call. The openai client's own retries honour `Retry-After` (3.00 s apart, the counter going 0→1→2), but the two waits between retry groups are **5.16 s** and **14.82 s** — with `RETRY_WAIT=2` those should have been 2 s and 4 s if the schedule started at `wait_seconds`, or 3 s if the header had been used. Neither wait relates to the `Retry-After: 3` the server sent.

Raw data (public, reproducible): `evidence/e0-retry-after/ra3_smol.jsonl`, `r429.py` (the server) and `NOTE.md` in https://github.com/simin-yuan/agent-double-exec-bench.

## Why it matters

On a 429 with a short `Retry-After`, the agent stays blocked for minutes when the provider was ready in seconds. With `max_attempts=3` and the default 60 s base, the worst case is 20 minutes of wall-clock for one call, which is longer than most CI jobs and than most people's patience with a CLI.

Related but different: #2586 reports that `wait_seconds` defaults to `0.0` (so backoff is off) and that `reraise` has no effect — that is about the default value and the error path. This one is about the schedule when a wait *is* configured, and about ignoring a server-declared cooldown.

## What I'd expect

- If the server sends `Retry-After`, sleep that long — and never sleep less than the server asked for.
- If the doubling before the first sleep is intentional, a comment saying so would help: as written, `wait_seconds` means "half of the first wait", which is easy to misread. If it isn't intentional, the first retry should wait `wait_seconds` and doubling should start after that.

## Status

A patch with five tests is ready locally (first-retry delay, jitter bounds, `Retry-After` honoured, opt-out flag, fallback when the header is absent). I have not opened a PR: I have one open PR (#3036) and I'll follow the one-open-PR rule until it lands. Happy to post the diff here, or to open the PR as soon as the issue is accepted and #3036 is resolved — whichever the maintainers prefer.

---

*Disclosure: I used an AI assistant to help draft this issue and to write and run the patch. I have read the change, run the tests, and will answer review comments.*

@@ -17,7 +17,7 @@
 import re

-from collections.abc import Generator
+from collections.abc import Callable, Generator
 from copy import deepcopy
 from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
 from enum import Enum
@@ -1704,6 +1704,24 @@ def create_client(self):
 
         return openai.OpenAI(**self.client_kwargs)
 
+    def _completions_create(self) -> Callable:
+        """Return the `chat.completions.create` callable for one `self.retryer` call.
+
+        The first attempt uses the client as configured, with its own retries. The retryer's replays use a copy
+        of the client with `max_retries=0`, so the two retry layers do not multiply.
+        """
+        attempt = 0
+
+        def create(**kwargs):
+            nonlocal attempt
+            attempt += 1
+            client = self.client
+            if attempt > 1 and hasattr(client, "with_options"):
+                client = client.with_options(max_retries=0)
+            return client.chat.completions.create(**kwargs)
+
+        return create

     def generate_stream(
         self,
         messages: list[ChatMessage | dict],
@@ -1724,7 +1742,7 @@ def generate_stream(

-            self.client.chat.completions.create,
+            self._completions_create(),
             **completion_kwargs,
             stream=True,
             stream_options={"include_usage": True},
@@ -1777,7 +1795,7 @@ def generate(
             **kwargs,
         )
         self._apply_rate_limit()
-        response = self.retryer(self.client.chat.completions.create, **completion_kwargs)

         content = response.choices[0].message.content

@@ -590,6 +590,70 @@ def test_stop_sequence_cutting_for_o4_mini(self):
             assert "<STOP>" not in result.content
             assert "and this should be removed" not in result.content
 
+    @staticmethod
+    def _mock_response():
+        response = MagicMock()
+        response.choices = [MagicMock()]
+        response.choices[0].message.role = "assistant"
+        response.choices[0].message.content = "Success response"
+        response.choices[0].message.tool_calls = None
+        response.usage.prompt_tokens = 10
+        response.usage.completion_tokens = 20
+        return response
+
+    def test_retry_replays_disable_client_retries(self):
+        """The client's own retries run on the first attempt only; the retryer's replays use max_retries=0,
+        so the two retry layers do not multiply."""
+        rate_limit_error = Exception("Error code: 429 - Rate limit exceeded")
+        with patch("openai.OpenAI"), patch("smolagents.models.RETRY_WAIT", 0):
+            model = OpenAIModel(model_id="test-model")
+        replay_client = model.client.with_options.return_value
+        model.client.chat.completions.create.side_effect = rate_limit_error
+        replay_client.chat.completions.create.side_effect = [rate_limit_error, self._mock_response()]
+        messages = [ChatMessage(role=MessageRole.USER, content=[{"type": "text", "text": "Hello"}])]
+
+        result = model.generate(messages)
+
+        assert result.content == "Success response"
+        assert model.client.chat.completions.create.call_count == 1
+        model.client.with_options.assert_called_with(max_retries=0)
+        assert replay_client.chat.completions.create.call_count == 2
+
+    def test_retry_replays_disable_client_retries_stream(self):
+        rate_limit_error = Exception("Error code: 429 - Rate limit exceeded")
+        event = MagicMock()
+        event.usage = None
+        event.choices = [MagicMock()]
+        event.choices[0].delta.content = "Success response"
+        event.choices[0].delta.tool_calls = None
+        with patch("openai.OpenAI"), patch("smolagents.models.RETRY_WAIT", 0):
+            model = OpenAIModel(model_id="test-model")
+        replay_client = model.client.with_options.return_value
+        model.client.chat.completions.create.side_effect = rate_limit_error
+        replay_client.chat.completions.create.return_value = iter([event])
+        messages = [ChatMessage(role=MessageRole.USER, content=[{"type": "text", "text": "Hello"}])]
+
+        deltas = list(model.generate_stream(messages))
+
+        assert [d.content for d in deltas] == ["Success response"]
+        assert model.client.chat.completions.create.call_count == 1
+        model.client.with_options.assert_called_with(max_retries=0)
+        assert replay_client.chat.completions.create.call_count == 1
+
+    def test_first_attempt_keeps_client_retries(self):
+        """Without a replay the client is used as configured: success, or an error the retryer does not retry."""
+        with patch("openai.OpenAI"):
+            model = OpenAIModel(model_id="test-model")
+        model.client.chat.completions.create.side_effect = [self._mock_response(), Exception("Error code: 500")]
+        messages = [ChatMessage(role=MessageRole.USER, content=[{"type": "text", "text": "Hello"}])]
+
+        assert model.generate(messages).content == "Success response"
+        with pytest.raises(Exception, match="500"):
+            model.generate(messages)
+
+        assert model.client.chat.completions.create.call_count == 2
+        model.client.with_options.assert_not_called()
